findings.title: Custody as unsubstitutable refuge
findings.claim: The pericope makes the focus's divine custody more than supremacy: it is the shelter that cannot be replaced, routed around, or transferred.
findings.mechanism: At 18:27, the text joins an explicit denial of replacement with failure to find a refuge outside Him; those negated alternatives contact the focus's custody relation and change it from a superior status into non-substitutable shelter.
findings.reader_payoff: The collapse named by the focus can be felt as the point at which no substitute support remains, while the ordinary claim that authority belongs to God stays recoverable.
findings.containment: This is an attributed pericope resonance of custody and refuge; it does not turn every mention of unchanged words or shelter into a new lexical sense of walayah.

findings.title: Property as a failed imitation of custody
findings.claim: The garden owner's enclosure, water, yield, cohort, and permanence form a counterfeit self-sufficient custody that the focus exposes as failed.
findings.mechanism: The protected garden, internal water circulation, accumulated yield, supporting cohort, and claim of permanence combine into a system that appears to manage and secure itself; the focus's true custody declaration changes the garden from mere property into a failed imitation of that function.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the collapse answers more than ownership: it dismantles the whole arrangement that had seemed to provide its own protection and continuance.
findings.containment: The property-system image is an attributed reading of the assembled parable; it does not deny the garden's literal prosperity or make human ownership equal to divine custody.

findings.title: Truth that remains at the collapse point
findings.claim: The focus's al-haqq is sharpened by the pericope's earlier declaration that truth is from the Lord: after the owner's claims fail, God's authority is the reality that remains standing.
findings.mechanism: The context occurrence of al-haqq in 18:29 gives truth an attributed source in the Lord, and the focus occurrence qualifies God's walayah with the same exact-truth sense; their contact turns the focus's adjective into a local answer to the owner's failed claim.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear 'the true' as more than praise: it identifies the authority that remains real when the garden's apparent security has collapsed.
findings.containment: This native pericope finding uses the supplied truth contact and the focus's core exact-truth facet; it does not claim that the two clauses are grammatically identical or activate every haqq facet.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies exact Arabic for 18:29 and 18:44, the authored connection, and the accepted focus facet, but the context-side morphology is surface evidence and the HFT provenance is legacy_unbound.
